scope: Observed Linux SDL display-library lifetime triage, not full game rendering
method: Executed only checksum-verified Actions binaries; sampled /proc/child/maps during life to attribute allocating PCs after dynamic-library unload. All leak checks stayed enabled.
decision: Use normal ELF-linked display dependency ownership for the Linux baseline; retain dynamic loading as an explicit diagnostic profile.
x11_disposition: Dynamic SDL-only report exactly reproduces earlier shell 50184 bytes/914 allocations. Immediate callers map to libX11 and Mesa Gallium. Linked SDL-only control (1 and 8 cycles) and original-data shell (two launches) exit 0 with empty stderr.
wayland_disposition: External Fontconfig/GTK-Pango/libdecor decoration allocation report: reproduces in SDL-only control even without any renderer. All 105 recorded allocation groups have an immediate Fontconfig caller. Retained as a failing Wayland LeakSanitizer observation, not counted as a clean run or suppressed.
limits: This uses the host GNOME Wayland session with X11 through Xwayland; no other compositor/driver is inferred.
Normal linked dependencies keep their process-global state mapped until process exit; no global-cache cleanup, dlclose wrapper, leak suppression or disabled detector was used.
Mapping identifies the allocating module; stripped system libraries do not provide complete internal source-line attribution.
The remaining Wayland report is outside the selected clean X11 sanitizer baseline; wider Wayland lifecycle coverage remains later validation.
